title: The Tot Signal
logline: Lily's earnest high-school ex Scooter is assigned to her school cafeteria, and one 'thanks' for extra tater tots becomes, in his mind, a sign. Every gentle letdown makes it worse, and Marshall's man-to-man talk ends with Scooter as his new best friend, while Robin bets Ted and Barney that they misread signals just as badly, with a brown suit and red tie for the loser.
coldOpen: Kids, in the fall of 2012, your Aunt Lily said two words to a man in a hairnet. It took her a month, your Uncle Marshall and about four hundred tater tots to take them back.

guests.name: Marnie Labelle
guests.role: a tourist from Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, on the wrong train; relentlessly polite, smiles at absolutely everything and apologizes to people, poles and doors alike

scenes.summary: Scotch night at Barney's. Lily reveals Scooter has been assigned to her school cafeteria, and her one 'thanks' for extra tots is now a sign. Cutaway: Scooter's version as told to the kitchen staff. Robin says every man reads signals like Scooter; Barney the 'signal sniper' and Ted the universe-reader object, and Robin bets them: first to misread a signal wears a brown suit and red tie to MacLaren's. Marshall volunteers to handle Scooter man to man. Lily reminds him what happened with the plumber.

beats.line: That fall, Barney made us drink at his place, because his scotch was better than MacLaren's.
Gentlemen. Robin. Lily. This scotch is older than all of Ted's relationships combined.
That is not even close to true.
It says aged three years.
So, close.
Guess who the district just assigned to my school cafeteria.
Bigfoot?
Worse. Scooter.
Wait. Aunt Lily dated a guy named Scooter?
It was the nineties, Penny. Half the boys at her school were named after something with wheels.
On his first day, he gave me extra tater tots. And I said two words. Thanks, Scooter.
So?
So now it's a sign. He told the whole kitchen. Doreen, the dishwasher, gave me his version.

beats.label: Scooter's version, as told to the kitchen staff

beats.line: Scooter. Thank you. For the tots.
It was nothing, Lily. They're just tots.
No, Scooter. They're extra tots.
Marshall never gives me extra tots.
I give you extra tots all the time! I give you all of my tots, Lily!
Since then he's re-laminated my alphabet, chaperoned a field trip nobody was taking, and he calls me Miss Aldrin.
Really leaning on the Miss.
Lily, that's not Scooter. That's every guy. You all hear thank you as take me.
Excuse me. I don't misread signals. I am a signal sniper.
Last week you thought a woman was into you because she held a door.
For four seconds, Robin. Three seconds is polite. Four seconds is a hotel key.
Well, I don't read women. I read the universe.
That's worse. That's Scooter with a telescope.
Yesterday a pigeon landed on my drafting table. Robin, pigeons mate for life.
It ate your eraser.
Meaningfully. It ate it meaningfully.
Bet. First one of you to misread a signal this week dresses like Scooter. Brown suit, red tie, MacLaren's, all night.
Brown? Robin, brown is the color of giving up.
Technically, it's an earth tone.
Exactly. The earth. Which everybody walks on.
And if neither of you slips up, I'll wear it.
Challenge accepted.
Lilypad, let me handle Scooter. Man to man.
Absolutely not. Remember when you went to fire our plumber?
Dmitri? Great guy. Beautiful wedding.
You were the best man, Marshall. You went to fire him and you gave a toast.
That was different. Dmitri had nobody.
Just promise me you won't come home with a best friend.
Lilypad, I'm a grown man. I already have a best friend.
My dad.
I drove you to Minnesota, Marshall. Twice.

scenes.summary: Lily ambushes Scooter on his self-assigned Wednesday shopping run and tries three gentle letdowns: stop the tots (he'll hide them under her salad), friends (that's how she and Marshall started, so he's behind schedule), married (he'll wait). Marshall sends Lily to the drinks fridge and goes man to man. They bond over Lily, then Scooter asks the two forbidden questions: Bigfoot and hunger. Marshall leaves with him. Thursdays are now theirs. Lily's button: he didn't even look back.

beats.line: Your Aunt Lily decided to let Scooter down gently. Your Aunt Lily has never done anything gently.
Scooter does the cafeteria's shopping here every Wednesday. Nobody asked him to.
Lilypad, how do you know his schedule?
He slid it under my classroom door. Laminated.
Lily! What are the odds?
Pretty good, Scooter. You gave me the schedule.
And you came anyway.
Scooter. I need you to stop giving me extra tots.
You're right. People are talking. I'll hide them under your salad.
Okay. Scooter, you're a great guy. And I see you as a friend.
A friend! That's how it started with you and Marshall!
We made out the night we met, buddy.
So we're behind schedule. Good to know.
Scooter, I'm married!
I know. And I respect that. So I'll wait.
Wait for what?
I'd rather not say it out loud. It's a little dark.
Did he just get in line behind my funeral?
That was me being gentle.
Lilypad, go wait by the drinks. I'm handling this. Man to man.
Scooter. Man to man.
Wow. Nobody ever talks to me man to man. It's usually lunch lady to man. I'm the lunch lady.
Lily is my wife. I love her more than anything in the world.
Me too.
Yeah. That's the problem, buddy.
Does she still get paint on her nose and not notice for a whole day?
A whole day! She taught a class with a blue nose!
Why are they smiling?
Okay. Focus. You need to back off.
Totally. Can I ask you something, man to man?
Do you believe in Bigfoot?
Kids, there are two questions you should never ask your Uncle Marshall. Does he believe in Bigfoot, and is he hungry. Scooter asked both.
I saw him once. New Jersey, 1996. Behind a seafood buffet.
Behind the buffet. Of course. That's exactly where I'd be.
Also, I've got a cooler of double-fried tots in my car. Are you hungry?
Scooter. I'm always hungry.
Lilypad! Great news! He's never going to bother you on Thursdays again!
Why not?
Because Thursdays, he's with me.
Eighteen years he follows me around. He didn't even look back.

scenes.summary: Montage: Marshall and Scooter become best friends. On the subway, Lily tells Ted, Robin and Barney about the handshake and Scooter's text: he thinks Marshall gave him his blessing. Ted is wounded about Thursdays. Barney reads a woman's three-signal salute, Ted reads a Gaudi biography as the universe; both approach; she's a polite Canadian who's been trying to see the map behind their heads. Double Scooter. Lily decides to give the no herself and practices on the gang. Robin says no back.

beats.line: Marshall had gone in to set Scooter straight. He came out with a Thursday.

beats.label: Marshall and Scooter, man to man

beats.line: The secret is, I double-fry everything.
Bigfoot documentary, part six!
And then we both go, rawr.
They have a handshake now, Ted. At the end, they both pretend to be Bigfoot.
Marshall and I have worked on our handshake for sixteen years. It's still not done.
And they have Thursdays? I never even thought to claim a weekday.
It gets worse.
He thinks my husband gave him his blessing.
beats.title: Scooter

messages.text: Marshall told me to take care of you. I will. Always.
He said take care, Scooter. Like goodbye.
He said it with his eyes.

beats.line: In fairness, Marshall says everything with his eyes. He once asked me to pass the salt and I cried.
Classic Scooter. Some of us can actually read signals.
Redhead, by the window. Two smiles, one hair touch, and a glance at my tie. That's a three-signal salute.
No, look what she's reading. A biography of Gaudi. On my train. The universe is basically shouting.
You're both doing it right now. In real time.
Hi. I got your signals. Barney.
Hi, I'm Ted Mosby, architect. I got your Gaudi.
Oh my gosh, sorry! Sorry! I've been trying to see the map behind your heads for six stops. Is this the express?
And the smiling?
Oh, I smile at everything. Sorry.
Let me guess. Saskatchewan.
Moose Jaw! Sorry!
Canadians smile at everything, boys. Mailboxes. Weather. Bears, right before they eat us.
You never smile at anything.
Some of us got through the winters with scotch.
This is me! Sorry! Sorry, pole!
That doesn't count. Canadians are a loophole.
Brown suits. Both of you.
That's it. Marshall can't say no to Scooter. So I'm going to do it myself. A real no. Tomorrow night.
Lily, you've never said no without that little evil smile.
Then I'll practice.
No.
I didn't ask you anything.
And yet it felt amazing.
No.
Oof. I really felt that one.
Wow. I see why Robin does this all the time.
No.

scenes.summary: Ted and Barney pay the bet in brown suits and red ties. Marshall brings Scooter, who reads the suits as a tribute. Lily gives him the real no; Scooter starts reading her eyebrows, and Marshall, as his friend, tells him it's a no and he'll be okay. Scooter is relieved, like taking off a hairnet. Heart, then the undercut: Lily's portion drops to nine tots and she tries to take the no back. Scooter doesn't read into it. Then Robin overreads Scooter asking about the last tot and loses her own bet.

beats.line: I want it on the record. I look incredible in brown.
You look like a pinecone at a job interview.
What about me?
The pinecone's dad.
Okay. They're coming up. No smile. No tots. Just no.
Hey, guys! Scooter brought tots!
Oh. Is this a Thursday thing? Nobody told me there was a Thursday thing.
Whoa. You guys dressed like me.
Is this a sign?
It's a punishment.
That's a kind of sign.
Scooter. I need to tell you something, and I need you not to read into it.
I would never. But you did wear earrings to tell me, so—
No.
No what?
No to all of it. The tots. The laminating. The waiting. Not now, not ever, not even if Marshall gets eaten by Bigfoot.
He'd never. He's a vegetarian.
Okay. But you said never with your eyebrows kind of up, and in my experience—
Scooter. Buddy. Look at me.
I've been married to that face for years. That's not a sign. That's a no.
A real no?
The realest. I should've told you on day one. I was too busy eating your tots.
But that's what a friend's for. Somebody's got to tell you the no. And then stick around after.
Huh. I've been reading signs since tenth grade. Nobody ever just told me.
It's kind of a relief. It's like taking off a hairnet.
Sorry about the laminating, Lily.
Don't be. The laminating was great.
Okay. So from tomorrow, you get the regulation portion. Nine tots.
Nine? I've been getting thirty since September!
Lilypad, that's what a no costs.
I take it back! Scooter, I take back the no!
I'm not going to read into that.
Robin. Can I ask you something? I've been wanting to all night.
Scooter, you're sweet. But I don't do rebounds. I barely do bounds.
I was going to ask if you wanted the last tot.
Robin Scherbatsky just got Scootered! Brown suit!
Fine. It's an earth tone.
Robin wore the brown suit the next night. Scooter told her it looked great, and didn't read a thing into it.
Kids, Scooter still works at that school. To this day, Aunt Lily gets nine tots. And every Thursday, Uncle Marshall gets thirty.
